item.observed: boomdrop-winner.png contains the crew and kit name but no kit URL.
item.title: Winning crews' downloaded picture cards do not show their kit link — the canvas renderer never draws the featured clip's URL

item.observed: With no qualifying clip, no clip-of-week-banner or Be this week's winner prompt is rendered.
item.title: Visitors with no clips posted this week see no winner invitation — the wall renders the banner only when clip_of_week exists

item.observed: A winner without kit_id shares the app's homepage rather than omitting a kit link.
item.title: Share-card recipients without a linked kit are sent an unrelated home link — the share URL falls back to the site origin

item.observed: After one featured video errors, a newly featured clip still shows the video-error fallback.
item.title: Visitors cannot open the next featured video after a broken winner changes — the banner retains its previous broken state across clip IDs

item.observed: A second phone behind the same NAT gets 429 while another phone uploads.
item.title: Crews sharing one network cannot upload at the same time — the upload guard treats their shared IP as one client

item.observed: Each distinct-IP request reads up to 60 MB before waiting for one of two transcode slots.
item.title: Visitors can still lose wall and builder responsiveness during many uploads — the two-slot transcode queue holds unbounded full video bodies in memory

item.observed: A newer or more-liked qualifying clip beyond the first 500 cannot be featured.
item.title: Visitors can still see the wrong weekly winner or no fresh drop after the wall grows — the changed selector filters only the first 500 unsorted approved clips

item.observed: GET /api/clips clip objects contain crew but omit crew_name.
item.title: Wall API consumers still cannot identify clip crews by crew_name — the changed featured and list responses return only the stored crew field

item.observed: A failed like silently reverts on reload and leaves an unhandled promise rejection.
item.title: Visitors still cannot tell that a like failed — the changed handler reloads in finally without catching or reporting the failed POST

item.observed: A failed admin list request displays Nothing to review or No clips are live yet.
item.title: Reviewers still see a false empty queue or live list when loading fails — the changed tab loader converts every error to an empty array

item.observed: Live on the wall lists only the newest 200 approved clips.
item.title: Reviewers cannot remove older mistakenly approved videos once more than 200 are live — the new live tab uses a capped list with no pagination

item.observed: Navigating away does not cancel the in-flight POST; it can still create a pending clip.
item.title: Uploaders can leave the page but still post a video they meant to abandon — the upload request has no abort signal or unmount cleanup

item.observed: A popup-blocking browser may block window.open after the asynchronous drawCard call.
item.title: Winning crews can get no Telegram share tab even though the app says their card was saved — the popup opens only after asynchronous font and PNG generation

item.observed: A 429 displays English: One upload at a time. Wait for your last video to finish.
item.title: Khmer-speaking uploaders receive English rejection reasons instead of a localized explanation — the upload panel displays raw server detail for 413 and 429

item.observed: Parallel POSTs with distinct forwarded addresses bypass the same-client 429 check.
item.title: A single client can bypass the parallel-upload guard and queue many videos — it trusts the caller-controlled X-Forwarded-For header as the phone identity

item.observed: A late pending response can populate the Live on the wall tab with pending clips.
item.title: Reviewers can reject a waiting clip believing it is live — tab responses are applied without checking which status is currently selected

item.observed: Opening the live tab starts full authenticated video downloads for up to 200 clips.
item.title: Reviewers can see the live tab stall or exhaust mobile data as clips accumulate — every card fetches its whole video immediately instead of loading on demand

item.observed: GET /api/clips returns featured_kind: null when no clip qualifies, not "none".
item.title: Wall API consumers cannot distinguish the specified no-winner state by its documented value — the selector returns null instead of none

item.observed: Oversize selection says Couldn't upload that video, not that the file is too large.
item.title: Crews choosing an oversized video are given a generic upload failure instead of a clear size warning — the pre-check reuses uploadFail

item.observed: A valid streamed multipart POST without Content-Length receives 411 before upload.
item.title: Streaming clients cannot submit otherwise valid shoot videos — the new guard rejects every request without Content-Length rather than enforcing a streamed byte limit

item.observed: A slower first metadata check can post an earlier file after a replacement was chosen.
item.title: Crews can still submit the wrong shoot video after choosing a replacement — the changed uploader remains enabled while metadata checks run

item.observed: An unreadable or timed-out duration falls through to send(f, "full") without a warning.
item.title: Crews can still post long footage without the required choice — the changed uploader treats unreadable duration as a short video

item.observed: Building or opening an eleventh kit removes the oldest from the upload selector.
item.title: Crews still cannot link older device-built kits to shoot videos — the changed upload panel reads a history capped at ten

item.observed: A long upload without keep defaults to full and does not require a length choice.
item.title: Crews can still post long videos without choosing their length — the changed upload route defaults missing or invalid keep to full

item.observed: A failed Mongo insert after put_object leaves the uploaded footage in storage.
item.title: A failed video post still leaves private footage stranded in cloud storage — the changed upload stores the object before inserting the clip without rollback

item.observed: Retrying after a lost response creates a second pending clip with a new id.
item.title: Crews can still submit duplicate videos after a lost upload response — the changed server creates a fresh ID on every retry without an idempotency key

item.observed: Missing or blank crew is accepted and saved as Phnom Penh crew.
item.title: Crews can still post under the wrong name — the changed upload route accepts a missing or blank crew and substitutes Phnom Penh crew

item.observed: Navigating away does not cancel the upload; server processing can still create a pending clip.
item.title: Uploaders can leave the page but still post a video they meant to abandon — the client never aborts and the upload handler does not stop on disconnect

item.observed: If PNG preparation outlasts transient activation, navigator.share rejects and no sheet opens.
item.title: Phone users can lose the winner sharing sheet when card preparation is slow — Web Share is invoked only after awaiting fonts and PNG encoding

item.observed: An older clip-list response can overwrite newer counts and rankings after two likes.
item.title: Visitors can still see stale winner standings after quick likes — the changed like handler starts overlapping refreshes without ordering their responses

item.observed: The approved and pending tab queries lack (status, is_deleted, created_at) sorting index.
item.title: Reviewers' new live tab and pending queue slow as clips accumulate — their status and deletion filter plus created_at sort lacks a compound index

item.observed: A moderation response arriving while the next tab is loading calls null.filter.
item.title: Reviewers can lose the admin screen when they switch tabs during moderation — the success update filters a null loading state

item.observed: Remove from wall immediately rejects the clip, with no confirmation or undo.
item.title: Reviewers can accidentally remove a crew's live clip and its likes with one tap — the new destructive control has no confirmation and rejected clips cannot be reapproved

item.observed: Fresh drop says No likes yet this week while top crews can show recent likes.
item.title: Visitors see contradictory weekly-like messages — the fresh banner says there are no likes even when older clips have recent likes

item.observed: A winner-sharing error displays Couldn't post the clip. Try again.
item.title: Crews are told their clip post failed when winner sharing fails — the share handler reuses the posting error message

item.observed: Two server workers each allow two transcodes and keep independent upload-IP sets.
item.title: Crews on multiworker deployments can run more than two transcodes and bypass the one-upload limit — both new guards are process-local

item.observed: A video fetch completing after a tab switch creates an object URL that is never revoked.
item.title: Reviewers can steadily lose browser memory while switching video tabs — late video fetches allocate blob URLs after their cleanup has already run

item.observed: Oversize selection says Couldn't upload that video, not that the file is too large.
item.title: Crews choosing an oversized video are given a generic upload failure instead of a clear size warning — the pre-check reuses uploadFail

item.observed: Fresh drop says No likes yet this week while top crews can show recent likes.
item.title: Visitors see contradictory weekly-like messages — the fresh banner says there are no likes even when older clips have recent likes

item.observed: A winner-sharing error displays Couldn't post the clip. Try again.
item.title: Crews are told their clip post failed when winner sharing fails — the share handler reuses the posting error message

item.observed: Missing crew or a crew_name-only request is saved as Phnom Penh crew.
item.title: Crews can still post under the wrong name — the changed upload route ignores crew_name and substitutes Phnom Penh crew for missing or blank crew

item.observed: Successful navigator.share completes without a winner-share confirmation toast.
item.title: Phone users receive no in-app confirmation after sharing the winner card — only the desktop download branch shows a toast
